title: The Skip-Count Star Vault
academicTheory: Assignment targets two distinct sub-skills bundled under "multiplication": (1) automatic recall of x2/x5/x10 facts, and (2) translating equal-groups word problems (boxes of pencils, rows of stars) into multiplication sentences. Both need direct, comparable practice today. Reina's engagement theory (evidenceCount 23+, confidence ~0.73-0.92) shows strong positive weight for puzzle (5.0) and speed (5.0) framing, near-zero/negative for competition, control, calm, and generic quiz shells (generated-baseline: 20% completion, dislike, frustration 0.554). Per Keller's ARCS and the child's own nextExperiment (variable: mechanic, arms unset), this board holds academic targets/question count/difficulty/evidence contract constant across two routes while varying MECHANIC (puzzle-lock manipulation vs. timed-speed run) to test which drives higher completion/engagement without adding competitive pressure or heavy control demands.

boardWorld.title: The Skip-Count Star Vault
boardWorld.narrative: Deep beneath an old observatory, a vault of frozen starlight has locked away its glittering treasure using ancient multiplication seals. Reina has found two entrances carved into the vault door: a Puzzle Gate of interlocking gears and a Comet Gate that only opens for those who move at comet-speed. Both paths lead to the same starlit treasure room, but only one gate will open first tonight.
boardWorld.backgroundPrompt: A glowing underground vault carved from deep indigo stone, dotted with softly pulsing star-shaped crystals and faint gold multiplication symbols etched into archways. Two ornate stone gates stand side by side: a left gate covered in interlocking bronze gears, and a right gate shaped like a comet trail with streaking light lines. Warm lantern light, soft particle sparkles, whimsical storybook-painterly style, no text.

fork.question: Which gate should we open first?
fork.hypothesis: Given her positive weights for both puzzle (5.0) and speed (5.0), Reina will complete either route, but comparing completion rate, replay choice, and frustration between the two mechanics will tell us which single mechanic to scale up next, since generic non-puzzle/non-speed shells (generated-baseline) have already failed her (0.2 completion).

difficulty (grade 3, single correct answer per item)

routes.label: Puzzle Gate
routes.promise: Rotate glowing gear-locks into place by solving each multiplication seal to crack open the vault gate.

routes.label: Comet Gate
routes.promise: Race a streaking comet across the sky, answering each seal before it passes to keep your speed trail lit.

activities.title: Gearlock Facts Chamber
activities.academicTarget: Recall multiplication facts for x2, x5, x10 (5 x 2, 5 x 5, 5 x 10, 2 x 7, 10 x 4)
activities.mechanic: Drag-and-rotate gear puzzle: child drags a numbered gear tooth onto the correct notch to complete each multiplication seal, then rotates the whole lock to confirm.

visualMock.scene: A round stone door segment shows five nested bronze gear rings, each ring engraved with a multiplication problem in its center hub and a ring of loose numbered teeth floating around its rim.
visualMock.layout: Center-screen circular gear mechanism (large), with a horizontal tray of 4 draggable numbered gear-teeth below it; problem text glows in the gear hub; a progress arc of 5 small star-crystals along the top fills as each gear locks.
visualMock.artworkPrompt: Close-up of an ornate bronze steampunk-fantasy gear lock embedded in indigo stone, glowing gold multiplication symbol in its center, loose numbered gear teeth floating nearby with soft light trails, warm lantern glow, whimsical painterly style, no readable extra text.

experience.objective: Solve all 5 fact problems by dragging the correct numbered gear-tooth into each gear's empty notch to fully lock the chamber door.
experience.childAction: Reina drags a floating numbered gear-tooth from the tray and drops it into the glowing notch on the current gear; she can rotate the gear slightly with a swipe to preview alignment before releasing.
experience.worldReaction: Correct tooth: the gear clicks into place with a satisfying chunk, spins once, and locks with a golden flash; a star-crystal on the progress arc ignites. Incorrect tooth: the tooth bounces off with a soft clank and gently floats back to the tray, the gear wobbles but does not break.
experience.anticipation: As each gear locks, the whole door mechanism hums louder and thin cracks of golden light spread outward, hinting the vault is close to opening.
experience.progress: 5 star-crystals along the top arc fill one by one; the gear door visibly brightens and the seams between stone panels glow wider with each solved gear.
experience.recovery: On an incorrect drop the tooth simply floats back to the tray with a gentle shimmer and a small owl guide character blinks encouragingly and whispers a hint like 'Try counting by 5s' -- no penalty, unlimited retries on the same gear.
experience.reward: All 5 gears lock simultaneously, the chamber door swings open in a burst of golden gear-dust and starlight, revealing a shimmering path forward; a chime plays and a 'Gate Cracked!' banner of light sweeps across the screen.

activities.title: Gearlock Story Vault
activities.academicTarget: Translate equal-groups word problems into multiplication (5 pencils x 4 boxes; 3 rows x 10 stars)
activities.mechanic: Drag-and-rotate gear puzzle applied to two story-scenario gears, where the child must first build the array visually (drag groups into place) then lock the matching answer gear.

visualMock.scene: Two large story-gears sit in a smaller inner vault room; each gear's hub shows a short illustrated scene (pencil boxes, star rows) with an empty answer notch, and a tray of numbered teeth below.
visualMock.layout: Two large gear panels side-by-side, each with an illustrated mini-scene at center (boxes of pencils / rows of stars) and a single answer notch beneath; draggable number teeth in a shared tray at bottom.
visualMock.artworkPrompt: Two ornate bronze story-gears in a glowing indigo stone vault room, one gear showing tiny illustrated pencil boxes arranged in rows, the other showing tiny glowing star rows, warm gold light, whimsical fantasy-steampunk painterly style, no readable extra text.

experience.objective: Read each story scene, determine the multiplication sentence it represents, and drag the correct total onto the gear's answer notch to unlock the inner vault room.
experience.childAction: Reina taps to reveal the illustrated scene animation (boxes filling with pencils, or stars arranging into rows), then drags the correct numbered gear-tooth onto the answer notch.
experience.worldReaction: Correct answer: gear locks with a golden flash, the illustrated scene glows and completes itself (all boxes full, all star rows lit). Incorrect answer: tooth clanks back to tray, the scene gently pulses to invite a recount without penalty.
experience.anticipation: As the first story-gear locks, a second illustrated gear panel slides into view, hinting a second scene puzzle to unlock the inner treasure alcove.
experience.progress: A 2-star mini progress arc above the gears fills as each story-gear locks; the inner vault room visibly brightens.
experience.recovery: An owl guide gently re-narrates the scene ('Count the boxes, then count what's inside each one') and the tooth floats back for another try, no time pressure.
experience.reward: Both story-gears lock, the inner vault alcove doors slide open revealing a glimmering treasure chest silhouette (locked for now) and a 'Story Solved!' light-burst plays.

activities.title: Comet Trail Facts Sprint
activities.academicTarget: Recall multiplication facts for x2, x5, x10 (5 x 2, 5 x 5, 5 x 10, 2 x 7, 10 x 4)
activities.mechanic: Timed sequential tap-run: a comet streaks across a starfield toward a seal; child taps the correct falling number-orb before the comet reaches it to keep the trail lit and advance to the next seal.

visualMock.scene: A horizontal starfield track where a glowing comet flies left to right toward a stone seal on the right edge; three number-orbs drift down from the top, one correct.
visualMock.layout: Wide horizontal comet-trail track spanning the screen, comet on the left animating toward the seal on the right; three tappable number-orbs fall in the mid-zone; a trail-light meter along the bottom shows how many seals are lit.
visualMock.artworkPrompt: A glowing comet with a long sparkling tail streaking across a deep-space starfield toward a glowing stone seal, three softly glowing number orbs falling mid-scene, vibrant blues and golds, dynamic motion-blur, whimsical painterly style, no readable extra text.

experience.objective: Tap the correct number-orb for each of the 5 fact problems before the comet reaches the seal, lighting all 5 trail segments to complete the sprint.
experience.childAction: Reina watches the comet approach and taps the falling orb showing the correct product; she can tap again immediately if she misses, since the comet loops back for another pass.
experience.worldReaction: Correct tap: the orb bursts into starlight, the comet's tail brightens and streaks forward, lighting a trail segment. Incorrect tap: the orb fizzles softly and the comet gently slows and loops back for a fresh pass, no crash or loss.
experience.anticipation: As trail segments light up, the comet's tail grows longer and more radiant, building visible momentum toward the final seal.
experience.progress: A 5-segment trail-light meter along the bottom fills as each correct tap lands; the comet visibly speeds up and glows brighter with each success.
experience.recovery: On a miss, the comet visibly eases off (no timer penalty), loops in a gentle arc, and re-presents three fresh orbs including the correct one, with a soft chime cue drawing attention to it.
experience.reward: The comet reaches the final seal with a full-lit trail, bursts into a shower of golden sparks across the starfield, and a 'Comet Cracked It!' banner streaks across the screen with a whoosh sound.
